motif.name: Nibelungs
motif.description: Passages of the piano score that match one melody, in levels by how close they are to it. Level 1 is the closest. A run of repeated notes counts as one note. Passages that overlap, or lie within 1 measure of each other, are joined into one; the level is that of the closest.

source.author: J. K. Holman
source.title: Wagner's Ring: A Listener's Companion & Concordance
source.publication: Portland, Oregon: Amadeus Press, 1996; paperback 2003, ISBN 978-1-57467-070-7

levels.label: Original
levels.name: The melody as given
levels.description: The melody as you gave it. It is not a passage of the score.

levels.name: Closest to the original
levels.description: The best partial matches of the whole phrase. The pitches and the rhythm are the same, in any octave.

levels.name: Same core pitches
levels.description: Notes 1 to 18 of the phrase have the same pitches, in any octave, but the rhythm differs. In a sung passage the score may have one short extra note between two of them: it is skipped.

occurrences.label: The original
occurrences.note: The melody as you gave it, engraved from your notes. It has no pickup, the bars are in 9/8, and the score has a treble clef and 5 flats in the key signature. It is not a passage of the score.

libretto.translation: We wait for him here.
Here! There! Hehe! Hoho!

libretto.text: Träges Heer! Dort zuhauf schichtet den Hort!
libretto.translation: Lazy host! Pile the hoard in a heap there!

libretto.text: Du da, hinauf! Willst du voran?
libretto.translation: You there, up! Will you go first?
Shameful people! Off with the jewellery!

libretto.text: Soll ich euch helfen? Alles hierher!
libretto.translation: Shall I help you? Everything here!

O shameful disgrace!
That the timid servants
see me gagged myself!
